rules.title: Downloaders set themselves up and say how far along they are
rules.contract: yt-dlp, spotDL and (on Windows) FFmpeg are set up without a prompt, in the background, into the app's own tools folder, and only after the file matches the SHA-256 its project published for that release. Each downloader row reads Setting up… with a named progress bar, Ready (adding "Set up automatically" when the app installed it), or Couldn’t set up: <reason> beside a Try Again button; the manual install advice appears only when the tool cannot be set up on this machine. Tools are set up one at a time, and one waiting its turn behind another also reads Setting up… — it is queued, not missing, so it shows no install advice and no badge. Only failed or unsupported tools count as missing — in the companion's Settings badge and on the player's Connections card, where a tool on its way reads "setting up". Where FFmpeg's absence explains an empty Tempo column, the Library says whether it is on its way or could not be set up.

rules.title: The look-ahead: the next picks’ previews, within a stated budget, never in the way
rules.contract: When the catalog's picks land, the next two picks that have a 30-second preview have it asked for ahead, so choosing one starts at once. The budget is stated and kept: two clips ahead at most, 4 MB held at most (measured from what arrived), one request at a time, each started only while the page is idle; a clip that will not come (no CORS, too large to be a clip) is streamed when chosen instead and never asked for again. Clips are held in memory as blob: URLs and let go once played or no longer among the next two; nothing is fetched while the catalog set is off, the browser asks to save data, or the device is offline. Whole songs are never fetched ahead: a fetch needs the person's statement of why they may have the file, made per song (NP-FIND-011). The UI never waits on the catalog or the look-ahead: the library's rows, the chip and Refresh answer while either is still out.
